title: Doubling Time Projection Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Calculate how many months a 50-minute task horizon takes to reach 40 hours for doubling times of 4, 5, and 6 months, then explore other doubling times and targets.

learningObjectives: The learner will calculate how many months a 50-minute task horizon takes to reach 40 hours for doubling times of 4, 5, and 6 months, to within one month, and describe how the answer changes with the doubling time.
prerequisites: Exponential growth, doubling time, number of doublings, trend extrapolation, and forecast uncertainty, from Chapter 5.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit three calculations before the controls unlock, then explore sensitivity
keyQuestions: How many doublings does the target need?
How far does the date move when the doubling time changes by one month?
commonMisconceptions: A small change in doubling time makes only a small change in the date
The time to reach a target is proportional to the target
assessmentOpportunities: Start 50 minutes, target 40 hours, doubling every 5 months. How many months?
The same at a 4-month and a 6-month doubling time?
Does 160 hours take four times as long as 40 hours?
Does a forecast have one answer?

controls.name: Your answer box and Check
controls.description: type a whole number of months and press Check (or Enter). Two attempts per question; only the first counts.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves on; after question 3 it unlocks the controls.

controls.name: Redo challenges and Defaults
controls.description: start the questions again, or reset to 5 months and 40 hours.
